title: Preventing pressure injuries

source.author: U.S. National Library of Medicine
source.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

body: Pressure injuries are also called bedsores, or pressure sores. They can form when your skin and soft tissue press against a harder surface, such as a chair or bed, for a prolonged time. This pressure reduces blood supply to that area. Lack of blood supply can cause the skin tissue in this area to become damaged or die. When this happens, a pressure injury may occur.
You will need to take steps to prevent these problems.
Eat enough calories and protein to stay healthy.
Drink plenty of water every day.
Ask your provider about creams or other medicines to help protect your skin in this area.

Make sure your wheelchair is the right size for you. Have your provider or physical therapist check the fit of your wheelchair once or twice a year, especially if you gain weight or feel pressure anywhere.
Sit on a foam or gel seat cushion that fits your wheelchair. Natural sheepskin pads are also helpful to reduce pressure on the skin. Do not sit on a donut-shaped cushions.
You or your caregiver should shift your weight (lean forward, left and right) in your wheelchair every 15 to 20 minutes. This will take pressure off certain areas and maintain blood flow.

If you transfer yourself (move to or from your wheelchair), lift your body up with your arms. Do not drag yourself. If you are having trouble transferring into your wheelchair, ask a physical therapist to teach you the proper technique.
